rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The third-person قال resumes the account and shifts from Moses’ quoted speech, framing what God answered after the two pleaded.
rows.anchor: إسناد الفعل إلى ضمير الغيبة كما قيل للاشعار بانتقال الكلام من مساق إلى مساق أخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tells them not to fear what they had mentioned about Pharaoh’s threat.
rows.anchor: لا تخافا ( مما ذكرتما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s presence means complete protection and aid; it explains the ban on fear and gives Moses and Aaron further reassurance.
rows.anchor: تعليل لموجب النهى ومزيد تسلية لهما والمراد بمعيته سبحانه كمال الحفظ والنصرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He understands an omitted object: whatever is said and done between them and Pharaoh, allowing them to repel harm and secure good.
rows.anchor: وهو بتقدير المفعول أى ما يجرى بينكما وبينه من قول وفعل

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal says this answers their fear that Pharaoh would not listen or would kill them: God hears their words and sees Pharaoh’s acts, preventing what they hate.
rows.anchor: وقال القفال : يحتمل أن يكون هذا فى مقابلة القول السابق

rows.speaker: الزمخشرى
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari estimates no object: God is protector and helper, and hearing and seeing complete the assurance; transitive verbs function intransitively.
rows.anchor: انا حافظ لكما وناصر سامع مبصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi finds al-Qaffal’s estimated-object account unpersuasive, while also reporting al-Zamakhshari’s objectless reading.
rows.anchor: فقدر المفعول أيضا لكنه كما ترى وقال الزمخشرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi rejects al-Tibi’s comparison with al-Mutanabbi: the verb is made intransitive here to complete the meaning of protection and aid.
rows.anchor: ويسمع واع على ما زعم الطيبى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse supports hearing and sight as attributes additional to knowledge: divine presence already implies knowledge, so this reading avoids redundancy.
rows.anchor: واستدل بالاية على أن السمع والبصر صفتان زائدتان على العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means to reach Pharaoh after being ordered to go, so it is not repetition; it coordinates with the preceding reassurance.
rows.anchor: أمر بإتيانه الذى هو عبارة عن الوصول إليه بعدما أمر بالذهاب إليه فلا تكرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They establish their mission at the outset so Pharaoh understands their standing; calling God their Lord is gentle, though Pharaoh may see it as belittling his claimed lordship.
rows.anchor: أمرا بذلك تحقيقا للحق من أول الأمر ليعرف الطاغية شأنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Release follows from their status as messengers; it means freeing Israel from captivity and abusive control, not ordering them to travel with Moses to Syria.
rows.anchor: ما بعدها على ما قبلها فان كونهما عليه السلام رسولي ربه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israel faced harsh digging, building, and stone-carrying labor; sons were killed in alternating years and women were put to service.
rows.anchor: فإنهم كانوا تحت ملكة القبط يستخدمونهم فى الأعمال الشاقة كالحفر والبناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation for beginning with release is gradual preaching: free the captives before changing Pharaoh’s belief.
rows.anchor: للتدريج فى الدعوة فإن إطلاق الأسرى دون تبديل الاعتقاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says freeing believers from unbelievers is more important; Alusi says this requires proof that Israel already believed in Moses or another prophet.
rows.anchor: تخليص المؤمنين من الكفرة أهم من دعوتهم إلى الإيمان وهذا بعد تسليمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A view says release clears an obstacle to Israel following Moses; Alusi objects that the context is calling Pharaoh and resisting his tyranny.
rows.anchor: لما فيه من إزالة المانع عن دعوتهم واتباعهم وهى أهم من دعوة القبط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says their first request was that Pharaoh believe, as indicated in al-Naziʿat; that request is omitted here because stated there, while release is omitted there because stated here.
rows.anchor: أول ما طلبا منه الأيمان كما ينبى عن ذلك آية النازعات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This explanatory resumption confirms their prophetic claim and explains why Pharaoh must obey: the sign establishes their mission.
rows.anchor: استئناف بيانى وفيه تقرير لما تضمنه الكلام السابق من دعوى الرسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating رب with Pharaoh addressed as its possessor reinforces the proof; قد marks certainty and emphasis, while construing it as expectation is strained.
rows.anchor: وجئ بقد للتحقيق والتاكيد ايضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular آية is used because the aim is one proof establishing their claim, not a count of separate proofs.
rows.anchor: وتوحيد الآية مع تعددها لأن المراد إثبات الدعوى ببرهانها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some identify the sign specifically as Moses’ hand; Alusi dismisses this identification.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المراد بالاية اليد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others identify the sign specifically as the staff; Alusi dismisses this identification too.
rows.anchor: وقيل : العصا والقولان كما ترى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here السلام means safety from punishment in both lives for those who follow guidance by affirming God’s signs; it is a verbal noun meaning safety, and على functions like لام.
rows.anchor: السلامة من العذاب فى الدارين لمن اتبع ذلك بتصديق آيات الله تعالى الهادية الى الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prepositions can exchange functions; على here also makes stylistic correspondence with the following العذاب على من كذب.
rows.anchor: وعلى بمعنى اللام كما ورد عكسه فى قوله تعالى ( لهم اللعنة ) وحروف الجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say their Lord revealed that worldly and otherworldly punishment falls on whoever denies God’s signs and turns away from accepting them.
rows.anchor: من جهة ربنا ( ان العذاب ( الدنيوى والأخروى ( على من كذب بآياته عز وجل

rows.speaker: الزمخشرى
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reads السلام as the greeting of Paradise’s keepers to the guided, with the Fire’s keepers implicitly reproaching and warning deniers; this promises the Garden and suits the exhortation.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشرى : أي وسلام الملائكة الذين هم خزنة الجنة على المهتدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi calls al-Zamakhshari’s interpretation far from the apparent meaning; safety from punishment already gives full encouragement and warning in both lives.
rows.anchor: وانت تعلم أن هذا التفسير خلاف الظاهر جدا وانكار ذلك المكابرة

rows.speaker: البحر
rows.claim: Al-Bahr calls al-Zamakhshari’s reading strange and says that taking punishment as for both lives and السلام as safety from it already fully encourages belief and warns against its opposite.
rows.anchor: وفي البحر هو تفسير غريب وانه إذا أريد من العذاب العذاب فى الدارين ومن السلام

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan takes this as a closing greeting, السلام as salutation, addressed to the guided to encourage Pharaoh to join them.
rows.anchor: والسلام فيه بمعنى التحية وجاء ذلك على ما هو العادة من التسليم

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan derives that Muslims should not greet unbelievers; if greeting is needed in speech or writing, use this formula.
rows.anchor: على منع السلام على الكفار وإذا احتيج اليه فى خطاب أو كتاب جئ بهذه الصيغة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Alusi cites the Prophet’s letter to Heraclius, beginning with سلام على من اتبع الهدى.
rows.anchor: ان رسول الله ( صلى الله عليه وسلم ) كتب إلى هرقل من محمد رسول الله

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says that when entering homes of People of the Book one should greet them with السلام على من اتبع الهدى.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة قال : التسليم على أهل الكتاب إذا دخلت عليهم بيوتهم أن تقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The greeting reading is plausible only if their speech ended at السلام; since they continue with revelation, both sentences are best taken as dictated, the latter explaining the warning.
rows.anchor: كلتا الجملتين من جملة المقول الملقن

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the dictated message ends at the sign and that the messengers themselves added the promise and warning afterward.
rows.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أن المقول الملقن قد تم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Murjiʾah infer that no one except unbelievers is punished at all.
rows.anchor: على أن غير الكفرة لا يعذبون أصلا وأجيب بأنه إنما يتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi replies this follows only if العذاب means all punishment; it can mean a particular or everlasting punishment, or hyperbolically general punishment that leaves room for finite punishment before endless safety.
rows.anchor: لم يلزم أن لا يعذب المؤمن المقصر فى العمل أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This oath-marked clause briefly recaps what happened between Moses and Pharaoh, emphasizing the importance of the account.
rows.anchor: حكاية أخرى إجمالية لما جرى بين موسى عليه السلام وفرعون عليه اللعنة وتصديرها بالقسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أرى may derive from visual perception or recognition, each originally taking one object and a second with the causative form.
rows.anchor: والأراءة من الرؤية البصرية المتعدية إلى مفعول واحد وقد تعدت إلى ثان بالهمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi rejects the knowledge verb analysis because it would require an impermissibly omitted third object in a reporting construction.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز أن تكون من الرؤية بمعنى العلم المتعدى إلى اثنين بنفسه وإلى ثالث بالهمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing the showing to God’s majestic plural magnifies the signs and Pharaoh’s persistence, and supports reading the preceding relative clause as God’s speech.
rows.anchor: وإسناد الأراءة إلى ضمير العظمة نظرا إلى الحقيقة لا إلى موسى عليه السلام نظرا إلى الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account says God showed Pharaoh the staff and hand after Pharaoh demanded proof, matching the earlier narrative of Moses’ signs.
rows.anchor: حين قال لموسى عليه السلام : ان كنت جئت بآية فأت بها إن كنت من الصادقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though there are two signs, Arabic may use the plural for a pair; alternatively, each miracle contains many remarkable details, each a sign.
rows.anchor: من بدائع الأمور التى كل منها آية بينة لقوم يعقلون

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: A report describes an eighty-cubit terrifying serpent; Pharaoh fled, a crowd crush killed twenty-five thousand, and he begged Moses by God who sent him to remove it, whereupon it became a staff again.
rows.anchor: فانه روى أنه عليه السلام لما ألقاها انقلبت ثعبانا أشعر فاغرافاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says the serpent rose a mile, swooped toward Pharaoh, and spoke to Moses; Pharaoh pleaded for its removal and it changed back into a staff.
rows.anchor: وروى انها انقلبت حية ارتفعت فى السماء قدر ميل ثم انحطت مقبلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’ hand shone with extraordinary luminous whiteness, brighter than the sun and drawing onlookers to marvel.
rows.anchor: بياضا نورانيا خارجا عن حدود العادات قد غلب شاعه شعاع الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since many details were not expressly listed, كلها stresses that Pharaoh saw every implication and detail, leaving no excuse.
rows.anchor: أريناه آياتنا بجميع مستتبعاتها وتفاصيلها

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some include the resolution of Moses’ speech impediment among the signs, as they do in God’s command to Moses and Aaron to go with His signs.
rows.anchor: وأدرج بعضهم فيها حل العقدة كما أدرجه فيها فى قوله تعالى اذهب أنت وأخوك بآياتى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A view attributed earlier to Ibn Abbas identifies these signs as Moses’ nine signs.
rows.anchor: التسع كما روى عن ابن عباس فيما تقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi objects that most of the nine appeared only after the magicians’ contest, some decades later; some destroyed rather than guided, and others came after Israel escaped.
rows.anchor: وفيه أن أكثرها إنما ظهر على يده عليه السلام بعد ما غلب السحرة على مهل

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Others take the possessive broadly to include miracles of all prophets, since Moses’ truthful report of them counts as showing them to Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: وعد آخرون منها الآيات الظاهرة على أيدى الأنبياء عليهم السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi objects that other prophets’ signs are not mentioned here and the coming account of magic and counter-challenge makes this reading unlikely.
rows.anchor: مما يبعد ذلك جدا وأبعد من ذلك كله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi calls it even more far-fetched to include Moses’ description of God’s deeds proving His exclusive lordship among the signs shown.
rows.anchor: وأبعد من ذلك كله إدراج ما فصله عليه السلام من أفعاله تعالى

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view takes the possessive as covering every kind of miracle, with كلها confirming all kinds were shown.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الإضافة لاستغراق الأنواع وكل تأكيد له

rows.speaker: السخاوى
rows.claim: Al-Sakhawi classifies miracles as creating what was absent, destroying what existed, or changing something while it remains.
rows.anchor: قال السخاوى : ترجع إلى إيجاد معدوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi says the staff and hand show these three categories, but questions whether they exhaust miracles and finds the proposal far-fetched even if they do.
rows.anchor: وفي الانحصار نظر ومع الاغماض عنه

rows.speaker: الكشفية
rows.claim: The Kashfiyya claim the signs were ʿAli shown to Pharaoh on a horse; Alusi calls the claim manifestly false despite their appeal to plural wording in 3:97.
rows.anchor: وزعمت الكشفية أن المراد من الآيات علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه أظهره الله تعالى لفرعون راكبا على فرس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ف marks immediate sequence; the omitted object is the signs or Moses, and Pharaoh denied without hesitation or delay.
rows.anchor: للتعقيب والمفعول محذوف أي فكذب الآيات أو موسى عليه السلام من غير تردد وتأخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He refused to accept the signs, truth, faith, or obedience, persisting in refusal to the utmost.
rows.anchor: قبول الآيات أو الحق أو الايمان والطاعة أى امتنع عن ذلك غاية الامتناع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most take his denial as deliberate rejection and arrogance, best fitting the condemnation; those who read أريناه as making him know the signs must likewise say he knowingly denied them.
rows.anchor: عند الأكثرين جحودا واستكبار وهو الأوفق بالذم ومن فسر أرينا بعرفنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What is in Moses’ right hand is his staff; the wording recalls God’s earlier question about what he held.
rows.anchor: عصاك كما وقع فى سورة الأعراف وكان التعبير عنها بذلك لتذكيره ما وقع

rows.speaker: بعض المحققين
rows.claim: Some scholars say ambiguity magnifies the staff as beyond familiar staffs and their ordinary effects, with strange consequences beyond human understanding.
rows.anchor: إنما اوثر الإبهام تهويلا لأمرها وتفخيما لشأنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same effect can be present when another passage narrates the order by meaning; this wording suits removing Moses’ fear and encouraging him.
rows.anchor: ووقع حكاية الأمر فى مواضع أخر بالمعنى والواقع نفسه ما تضمن هذه النكتة

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says right hand evokes good fortune and blessing; Alusi objects that the address to Moses was not in Arabic.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حيان : عبر بذلك دون عصاك لما فى اليمين من معنى اليمن والبركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the ambiguity as belittling the many ropes and staffs: a little stick will consume them; Alusi says this ignores the staff’s earlier extraordinary state.
rows.anchor: بأن المراد لا تبالى بكثرة حبالهم وعصيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما may be relative or descriptive; one analysis pairs the first possibility with the first construction and the second with the second.
rows.anchor: وما يحتمل أن ان تكون موصوفة ويحتمل أن تكون موصولة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority reading is jussive as an answer to the command; from لقف, it means to take deftly by hand or mouth, here by mouth, with feminine agreement because ما refers to the staff.
rows.anchor: بالفم وامراد هنا الثانى والتأنيث بكون ما عبارة عن العصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The staff swallows ropes and staffs whose motion only seemed real; calling them what the magicians made belittles them and signals deception.
rows.anchor: أي تبتلع ما صنعوه من الحبال والعصى التى خيل إليك سعيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers pronounce تلقف with an open lām and doubled qāf, dropping one of the two tāʾs from تتلقف.
rows.anchor: بفتح اللام وتشديد القاف وإسقاط إحدى التاءين من ( تتلقف

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAmir has the same form but raises the verb as a new explanatory clause or a circumstantial clause for the agent or object of ألق.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر كذلك إلا أنه رفع الفعل على أن الجملة مستأنفة استئنافا بيانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command completes the prohibition by explaining how Moses will prevail: the staff consumes the falsehood that triggered his hidden fear.
rows.anchor: وجملة الأمر معطوفة على النهى متممة بما فى حيزها لتعليل موجبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some argue this proves Moses did not fear people doubting the staff’s miracle, since the reply would otherwise promise their belief; Alusi says the argument merits consideration.
rows.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أن هذا صريح فى أن خوفه عليه السلام لم يكن من مخالجة الشك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This clause explains why the staff swallows their work; ما may mean what they made, a thing they made, or their making.
rows.anchor: وما إما موصولة أو موصوفة أو مصدرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the nominative reading, كيد ساحر is the predicate of إن; ساحر is indefinite so the genitive is likewise indefinite as the context requires.
rows.anchor: بالرفع على أنه خبر إن أى كيد جنس الساحر وتنكيره للتوسل به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though الساحر could be definite yet generic, there is no need to identify the magic’s kind: the preceding context does so and the point is its unreality.
rows.anchor: وأجيب بأنه لا حاجة إلى تعيين جنسه فانه مما علم من قوله تعالى ( يخيل ) الخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A proposal that indefiniteness belittles the trick is unsuitable, implies ranks of magic, and conflicts with their magic being called great; apparent greatness can coexist with inner triviality.
rows.anchor: لا يناسب المقام ولأنه يفيد انقسام السحر إلى حقير وعظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation makes الساحر indefinite to avoid the idea of a particular, known sorcerer.
rows.anchor: أن المراد ساحر معروف فتدبر

rows.speaker: مجاهد، حميد، زيد بن على
rows.claim: Mujahid, Humayd, and Zayd ibn ʿAli read كيد in the accusative as the object of صنعوا, with ما functioning as an expletive.
rows.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد وحميد وزيد بن على عليهم الرحمة ( كيد ) بالنصب على أنه مفعول

rows.speaker: حمزة، الكسائى، أبو بحرية، الأعمش، طلحة، ابن أبى ليلى، خلف، ابن عيسى الأصبهانى، ابن جبير الأنطاكى، ابن جرير
rows.claim: These readers have سِحْر with kasra on sīn and a still ḥāʾ: possessor of magic, a sorcerer called magic by intensification, or a genitive showing the trick is of magic’s kind.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائى وأبو بحرية والأعمش وطلحة وابن أبى ليلى وخلف فى اختياره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the explanatory genitive, the commentator of al-Hadi describes the relation as lām and al-Sharif’s apparent position as min; some require a particular overlap between terms.
rows.anchor: من إضافة العام الى الخاص وهى على معنى اللام عند شارح الهادى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No sorcerer succeeds wherever he may be; حيث is a place adverb used universally, completing the explanation for Moses’ command.
rows.anchor: حيث كان وأين أقبل فحيث ظرف مكان أريد به التعميم من تمام التعليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text does not say the staff is a divine miracle, although that could strengthen the reasoning, because its status is already evident.
rows.anchor: ولم يتعرض لشأن العصا وكونها معجزة الهية مع ما فى ذلك من تقوية التعليل

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report collected by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh from Jundub says the Prophet ordered that a sorcerer be killed when caught, then recited this verse; Alusi gives no grading.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله ( صلى الله عليه وسلم ) إذا أخذتم الساحر فاقتلوه ثم قرأ

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: One group reads أين أتى instead of حيث أتى.
rows.anchor: وقرأت فرقة ( اين اتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ف implies omitted events: fear ended, Moses cast the staff, it became a serpent and swallowed their ropes and staffs, then the magicians recognized the miracle.
rows.anchor: عن التصريح أى فزال الخوف وألقى ما فى يمينه وصارت حية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They fell prostrate to God in repentance, believing in God and in Moses’ mission.
rows.anchor: فألقى السحرة على وجوههم سجدا لله تعالى تائبين مؤمنين به عز وجل وبرسالة موسى

rows.speaker: رئيسهم
rows.claim: Their leader says they used to defeat people while their tools remained; asking where their objects went if this were magic, they inferred a powerful, knowing Creator and Moses’ true mission.
rows.anchor: روى أن رئيسهم قال : كنا نغلب الناس وكانت الآلات تبقى علينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They reasoned from bodily transformation to an omnipotent, knowing Creator and from the miracle through Moses to the truth of his prophethood; total annihilation is possible.
rows.anchor: فاستدل بتغير أحوال الأجسام على الصانع القدير العليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying they were made to fall, rather than simply that they prostrated, shows the sight overwhelmed them; the wording evokes God’s guidance from obstinate unbelief to faith.
rows.anchor: وفي التعبير بألقى دون فسجد إشارة إلى أنهم شاهدوا ما أزعجهم فلم يتمالكوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrasing also gives stylistic correspondence and conveys that they hurried to prostrate.
rows.anchor: وفيه إيقاظ السامع لألطاف الله تعالى فى نقله من شاء من عباده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is said they did not lift their heads until they saw the Garden and Fire, reward and punishment.
rows.anchor: من السجود حتى رأوا الجنة والنار والثواب والعقاب

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrimah reports that God showed them their Garden stations while they prostrated; al-Qadi objects this compels belief and undermines moral responsibility.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة أنهم لما خروا سجدا أراهم الله تعالى فى سجودهم منازلهم فى الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi replies that faith preceded the unveiling, so it did not compel them; al-Irshad says their stations were theirs in light of their plea for forgiveness.
rows.anchor: أجيب بأنه حين كان الإيمان مقدما على هذا الكشف فلا منافاة ولا إلجاء

rows.speaker: إرشاد العقل السليم
rows.claim: Al-Irshad says seeing their stations does not conflict with their plea for forgiveness, since the stations were theirs conditional on that declaration.
rows.anchor: ارشاد العقل السليم أنه لا ينافيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: قالوا is a resumption, as in earlier passages.
rows.anchor: استئناف كما مر غير مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses comes second because he is more honored and the mission belongs primarily to him; the miracle appeared through him and the order maintains the verse’s rhyme.
rows.anchor: تأخير موسى عليه السلام عند حكاية كلامهم المذكورة فى سورة الأعراف المقدم فيه موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possibility is that this was their actual order because Aaron was older; al-Sayyid’s claim that Moses was older is a mistake.
rows.anchor: وقدموا هرون عليه السلام بأنه أكبر سنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order may avert the false inference that رب موسى means Pharaoh, who raised Moses; the al-Aʿraf ordering is the narrator’s arrangement for this reason.
rows.anchor: وأما للمبالغة فى الاحتراز عن التوهم الباطل من جهة فرعون وقومه حيث كان فرعون ربى موسى

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan allows this and al-Aʿraf to quote two groups, each ordering the names for a different point; since their meanings match, both statements can be attributed to all. Alusi prefers this for this sūra.
rows.anchor: وجوز أبو حيان أن يكون ما هنا قول طائفة منهم وما هناك قول أخرى وراعى كل نكتة فيما فعل
